title: DR1 refuses to move on from the contact page until an address is chosen; the frontend accepts Save and continue with nothing selected.

finding.frontend: Pressing Save and continue with no radio chosen is allowed through. The page only rejects a value that is not one of the addresses offered, and the controller says so in as many words: the contact is mandatory as an obligation, but an empty submit returns the trader to the hub with the task simply incomplete (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:29-39). The trader is not told they have skipped anything at the moment they skip it; they find out later at the hub.
finding.prototype: DR1 validates the choice on submit and, when nothing is selected, re-renders the page with the error "Select a contact address" in the summary and against the radios (app/routes.js:1138-1155). There is no way past the page without answering it.
finding.difference: Make an empty submit on the contact page an error carrying the message the frontend already has for the case, rather than a silent pass. The message exists — contactRequired, "Select a contact address" — and is only reached today when a value outside the list is posted. Blocking at the page is already this journey's pattern rather than a departure from it: the frontend ships two validators for a radio group, and the origin, destination-country, port-of-exit and declaration pages all use the one that refuses an empty answer, while the contact page uses the permissive one that explicitly allows an empty string (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:100-121). So the work is one page moving onto the stricter of two validators the codebase already has, and it is not a decision about the whole journey.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting the frontend contact page with no radio selected and getting "There is a problem" rather than a redirect.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs for fe-contact and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment, the fe-contact screenshot, the frontend controller at the cited lines and the validator behind it, and DR1's validateContactAddress; could not run the falsifier, because neither side has an error-state capture of this page and the brief forbids starting either application, so the claim was settled from source on both sides. The frontend claim holds: `oneOf` is built as `Joi.string().allow('').valid('', ...values)` at src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:114-121, so an empty payload passes validation, `state.commit` is never called and the handler redirects. The hub is the right destination — contact is the only page in its flow section (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:78-79), so nextInSection has nothing to return. DR1's claim holds at app/routes.js:1139-1155. CORRECT, with the open question in `difference` now closed — see `correction`.
finding.correction: Claim stands; one open question in `difference` resolved and that sentence replaced. The author asked whether letting a trader leave a task part-done is a journey-wide rule that this page merely exposes, in which case the finding would point at the wrong fix. It is not. The frontend uses both validators side by side: `requiredOneOf` refuses an empty answer on origin (controller.js:65), destination-country (:32), port-of-exit (:34) and declaration (:26), and the permissive `oneOf` is used on contact, import-reason, import-purpose, transporter-type and transporters-select. Blocking at the page is therefore an existing pattern in this journey, not a new rule, and the fix named here is the right one. Confidence left at medium: the outcome is read from source on both sides and photographed on neither.
